clue.text: Club overhauls counselling and welfare, for example

parts.note: a social is a club or gathering held for members to meet and drink
services means overhauls, as a garage does to a car

explanation.surface: A club is being reorganised to provide counselling and welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is just the first piece of a simple charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Counselling and welfare are examples of the help provided by state social departments.

clue.text: Airing one's notes

parts.note: sounds like publicising your memos, but means voicing musical notes, giving an air

explanation.definitionFit: Producing musical notes with the voice, performing an air, is vocal performance.

clue.text: Skill of well-informed person somehow crushes opinions

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: An expert's skill somehow squashes other people's views.
explanation.definitionFit: A connoisseur is an expert judge, and the suffix makes the noun for that expert skill.

clue.text: Make good a wager

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Settling a bet honourably.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or support, here loosely the sense of making something good happen.

clue.text: Criminal started shooting at target area

indicators.note: started points to the letter that begins the word shooting

parts.note: the inner is the ring of a target next to the bull

explanation.surface: A gunman opened fire at a target zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner is a wrongdoer, broadly a criminal in the moral sense.

clue.text: Withdrawals from the refuges

definitions.meaning: acts of pulling back, as an army does
quiet places of shelter and seclusion

explanation.surface: Troops pull back from their shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both retreats from battle and peaceful hideaways where one shelters.

clue.text: Special ship that cuts through formalities!

definitions.meaning: a vessel built to force through frozen seas
a joke or activity that relaxes strangers at first meeting

explanation.surface: A vessel that slices through stuffy etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a ship clearing sea ice and anything that eases social stiffness.

clue.text: Conversation guide for tutor from abroad, perhaps

parts.note: an exchange is a conversation, a back-and-forth of words
a teacher guides pupils

explanation.surface: A phrasebook guide for a foreign tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange teacher swaps posts with a counterpart abroad, so is a visiting tutor from overseas.

clue.text: Crafty person's noisy domestic heater

indicators.note: noisy says we want a word said aloud like the slang for a man

parts.note: geezer is slang for a fellow, often a sly or wily one

explanation.surface: A cunning character's clattering home boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the domestic gas water heater is pronounced to match the slang for a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a geyser is a gas appliance heating water in the home.

clue.text: Grandmother avid about cotton material

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
keen means avid or eager

explanation.surface: A grandmother is enthusiastic about a particular cotton fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Large plant around a cold lake produces molasses

indicators.note: around tells us the big plant's letters go round the others

parts.note: a tree is a large plant
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
L is a common abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A big plant growing round a chilly lake yields molasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the British name for molasses, the dark syrup left from sugar refining.

clue.text: Club for the press

definitions.meaning: a golf club with an angled metal head
a household appliance used to press clothes smooth

explanation.surface: A golf club made for the journalists' tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a golf club with a metal head and the hot appliance used to press clothes.

clue.text: Tries again Alan's dummy runs

parts.note: rehears means tries a case again in court
Al is short for Alan, so Alan's gives AL plus S

explanation.surface: A judge retries Alan's case, as if it were a practice run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' has its legal sense: a court that rehears a case tries it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy runs are practice performances before the real thing, which is what rehearsals are.

clue.text: Advising wrongly on badly inlaid gems

indicators.note: badly means the gems are poorly set, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Giving bad advice about poorly set jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Misleading means giving a false impression, steering someone wrongly.

clue.text: Tittle-tattle concerning white china holiday mementos I personally originate

parts.note: Goss china is white porcelain crested souvenirs made in Stoke-on-Trent, popular as holiday keepsakes

indicators.note: originate asks for the letter where the word personally begins

explanation.surface: Chatter about seaside souvenir china that the speaker claims to have created.
explanation.walkthrough: Goss is crested souvenir china, white porcelain bearing town crests, sold to British holidaymakers from Victorian times.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter about other people, a close synonym.

clue.text: Alien park officer found on the way

indicators.note: found on places the officer after the road, attached to it

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
a ranger is an officer who patrols a park

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial and a park warden are discovered on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, someone unknown to us.

clue.text: Extricate from fashionable National maze

parts.note: U means upper-class or socially acceptable, as in U and non-U
a tangle is a maze or confused knot

explanation.surface: Getting out of a trendy national labyrinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U and non-U' was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus other usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free from a knot or tangle, so to unpick it.

clue.text: Legend in fancy sewing

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A myth embroidered in decorative needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling is working with a needle, as in sewing; the verb can mean to sew.

clue.text: Lower region above the clouds to the North

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for North
ether is the clear upper sky beyond the clouds

explanation.surface: A region of the north lying higher than the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to the North' puts N at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: 'L' is for 'hirer'

definitions.meaning: L is one character of the alphabet
one who lets property out, a landlord who rents it

explanation.surface: A child's alphabet book: L is for something.
explanation.definitionFit: L is an alphabet character, and someone who lets a house out for rent is one who lets it.

clue.text: Actively urge pro to join up again

indicators.note: actively suggests lively movement of the letters

explanation.surface: Energetically encourage a professional to rejoin.
explanation.definitionFit: To regroup is to gather together again after being scattered.

clue.text: Explosively blast a rock

indicators.note: explosively suggests blowing the letters apart and rebuilding them

explanation.surface: Blowing up a boulder with dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock.

clue.text: Sailor with two other men seen on the road

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman or any man
Adam is a man's name, the first man

explanation.surface: A sailor and two companions are spotted on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is the road surface of tar and stones, so it is seen on any road.

clue.text: Contacted the fruit centre

indicators.note: centre asks for only the middle of the fruit, its ends dropped

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone phoned the fruit market.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends O and E of ORANGE are removed, leaving its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang means telephoned, a way of contacting someone.

clue.text: X

parts.note: the mark written at the foot of a love letter or card

explanation.definitionFit: The cross sign at the end of a note stands for an affectionate peck on the lips.

clue.text: Repeatedly imitating a mountain nymph, in German

parts.note: Echo was the Greek mountain nymph who could only repeat others' words

explanation.surface: A mountain spirit mimicking voices in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoing means repeating sounds or words, imitating them over and over.

clue.text: I hoot as a result of a sneeze

indicators.note: a result of suggests the letters are produced by reworking the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone honks loudly because of a sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a result of' rearranges I HOOT AS; 'as' reads like part of 'as a result of' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the conventional written sound of a sneeze, standing for the sneeze itself.

clue.text: Pasta pieces tipped over on a dress

parts.note: spaghetti is a long thin pasta

indicators.note: tipped over in an across clue turns the word for pieces backwards

parts.note: parts means pieces

explanation.surface: Bits of pasta are spilt on someone's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin shoulder strap is found on a dress, especially an evening dress or slip.
